lead_with.title: Your group is already in Montreal
lead_with.text: **Crédit Agricole CIB** runs Canadian coverage from **Montreal and Toronto**. Indosuez would not be starting from zero: it would join an existing group footprint, in the **New York time zone** and in a **bilingual (French/English)** city.

lead_with.title: The cost case
lead_with.text: A Finance Montréal-commissioned 2026 study puts a 150-person financial operation at about **US$18.9M a year in Montreal vs US$35.3M in New York**. Quebec's **International Financial Centre (IFC) credit** covers **24% of eligible salaries, up to C$18,000 per employee per year** (minimum 6 eligible staff).

lead_with.title: Peers already there
lead_with.text: **BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole, State Street** and **Morgan Stanley** operate in Montreal: a ready talent pool for wealth, fund, compliance and middle-office work.

company.text: Indosuez Wealth Management is the wealth management arm of the **Crédit Agricole group** (Jacques Prost has been CEO since 2018), with roots in Asia going back to the **Banque de l'Indochine** offices in Hong Kong and Singapore. The Singapore branch belongs to **CA Indosuez (Switzerland) SA** and is supervised by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. Recent build-up: majority stake in **Degroof Petercam** (Belgium, 2024), absorption of **Banque Thaler** (Switzerland, Dec 2025) and purchase of BNP Paribas Wealth Management's **Monaco client book** (Mar 2026). In August 2026 Indosuez moved the global management of its **Advisory and Capital Markets** to **Singapore**, its Asia headquarters, under Asia CEO **Laurent Proutière**. North American presence of Indosuez itself **to be confirmed** (none found in Canada).

financials.country: France, part of Crédit Agricole S.A. (Euronext Paris: ACA)
financials.text: Indosuez: **€233bn AuM** at end-December 2025 (up 3.2% over Q4) with record Q4 net inflows of **€3.9bn**. A third-party profile cites about **€249bn AuM at June 30, 2026**, 2025 net income of **€170m** (+19.7%) and **4,300+ staff in 15 territories** (to be confirmed against Crédit Agricole's own reports). Parent **Crédit Agricole S.A.** FY2025: revenues **€28.1bn** (+3.3%), pre-tax income **€10.4bn** (-2.1%), with costs up 4.9%. Context: a growing, acquisitive business under **cost pressure**, which suits a cost-location pitch.
